_about: Field terms for F28, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

brier.definition: the squared difference between the stated probabilities and the outcomes, here summed over the answer options in the Good Judgment Project form so it runs from 0 to 2; lower is better
brier.excludes: questions left unanswered, which it does not score

relative-brier.definition: a forecast's Brier score minus the median Brier score of all scored survey forecasts on the same question; lower is better
relative-brier.excludes: the difficulty of the question, which subtracting the median removes

extremity.definition: the distance of a binary forecast from 50 percent, from 0 for a coin-flip forecast to 0.5 for a certain one
extremity.excludes: whether the forecast was right, and how well calibrated the forecaster is

forecaster-year.definition: one person's forecasts within one tournament year, the unit for every statistic here
forecaster-year.excludes: pooling of different people, and pooling one person's years

skip.definition: a closed question that was open during a forecaster's active window in a year and that they never answered, inferred from the data
skip.excludes: questions outside the active window, and any recorded decision to decline, which the data do not hold

stratum.definition: a group of units alike on the matched variables, here year and twentieth of forecast count, inside which a statistic is computed before averaging
stratum.excludes: control for variables that were not matched

spearman.definition: the correlation between the ranks of two quantities, from -1 to 1, which counts any steadily rising or falling relation and is not pulled by single extreme values
spearman.excludes: the slope of a relation, and evidence of cause

bootstrap.definition: recomputing a statistic many times on forecaster-years resampled with replacement to read how much the estimate varies
bootstrap.excludes: an interval from a textbook formula that assumes a distribution

cc0.definition: the Creative Commons public domain dedication, under which anyone may reuse the work for any purpose without permission
cc0.excludes: a licence condition requiring citation, which stays a scholarly courtesy

positive-control.definition: a test of an effect expected to be present, which the instrument must detect for its other readings to be trusted
positive-control.excludes: a shuffle control, which removes an effect instead
